stories.headline: EEAST reports record 999 demand in September
stories.body: The East of England Ambulance Service took nearly 100,000 999 calls and attended over 84,000 incidents in September, up from about 90,000 calls a year earlier. Crews lost more than 18,000 hours waiting to hand patients over.
stories.why: Rising demand plus handover delays means fewer crews free to respond, and longer waits for patients.

stories.headline: SECAmb pilots live video calls for cardiac arrests
stories.body: Since 26 October, SECAmb critical care paramedics can send callers a secure, unrecorded video link in a suspected cardiac arrest to see the scene, coach bystander CPR and brief crews before arrival. The pilot runs for four weeks.
stories.why: Seeing the scene early could improve bystander CPR. The trust hit its best-ever 30-day survival rate of 17.2% in May.

stories.headline: NEAS trials AI note-taking on crew iPads
stories.body: North East Ambulance Service is running an eight-week trial with 38 staff using ambient voice tech to record, transcribe and summarise patient conversations. Every note is checked by a clinician before it goes on the record.
stories.why: Less time on paperwork could mean more time with patients, but clinicians stay accountable for the record.

stories.headline: LAS signs deal to run its EV charging network
stories.body: As London Ambulance Service grows its electric fleet, Optimo Energy will manage more than 700 charging connectors, linking vehicle telematics and battery data so ambulances are charged and ready between jobs.
stories.why: Electric ambulances are coming, and keeping them charged is now part of keeping crews on the road.

stories.headline: SAS trains for resus in a packed nightclub
stories.body: Scottish Ambulance Service and fire crews ran resuscitation scenarios in an Edinburgh Cowgate bar, with loud music, darkness, haze and bystanders added to practise leading and communicating under pressure.
stories.why: Organiser and paramedic Steve Reiffer called it "stress inoculation": rehearsing chaos so real jobs feel calmer.
